newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand keeps sugar cane forecast at 62.42m tns.
newsitem.headline: Thailand keeps sugar cane forecast at 62.42m tns.

text.p: The Thai Agriculture Ministry kept its 1996/97 (November-October) sugar cane production forecast unchanged at its previous estimate of 62.42 million tonnes against 1995/96 output of 60.85 million tonnes, an official said on Friday.
The 1996/97 planting area was put at 1.07 million hectares versus 1.05 million hectares in the last crop year, she said.
"Our view is that the floods were not severe enough to affect sugar cane output," the official said.
"Last year the situation was much worse and Thailand still enjoyed a good cane crop," she added.
Thailand's monsoon season starts in late May, but in the past few weeks there has been severe flooding in some crop areas.
The official said the ministry's latest data was gathered before the flood situation deteriorated in many areas, however.
The Agriculture Ministry revises its forecasts on crop output every other month. The last time it revised its sugar cane output figure was in July, however.
Industry Ministry sources said earlier this week that the floods could reduce 1996/97 cane output to below 60 million tonnes.
